numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With jax_debug_nans enabled, calling jax.scipy.stats.gamma.pdf (vmapped, inside jit) raises FloatingPointError: invalid value (nan) encountered in jit(log), because the implementation produces internal NaNs even though invalid inputs (x < loc) should yield -inf.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: No NaN should be produced internally; invalid inputs such as x < loc should return -inf from gamma.logpdf without triggering the debug_nans check.
trigger_conditions: jax.scipy.stats.gamma.pdf is called, e.g. via jax.vmap, on inputs where x < loc
the call is executed under jit so the NaN is checked in the compiled function

input_output_examples.input: mle_loss(data, target) with jax_debug_nans=True, where target = jnp.array([1.0, 1.0004145, 0.99964607, 1.0004367, 1.000424, 0.99967706, 1.0009085, 1.000621]) and data rows have shape (batch, history, 3) with weights, k=data[:,:,1], theta=data[:,:,2]
input_output_examples.buggy_output: FloatingPointError: invalid value (nan) encountered in jit(log)
input_output_examples.expected_output: No FloatingPointError; invalid-input gamma densities evaluate to -inf without internal NaNs

oracle_clues: PR #25038 states that logpdf handles invalid inputs (e.g. x < loc) by returning -inf, but the existing implementation incorrectly triggers the NaN checks of deb

numerical_characteristics.tolerance: atol=1E-6 appears in the existing testGammaLogPdfZero check for gamma.pdf(0.0, 1.0) against scipy; the new regression test uses assertAllClose with default tolerances and does not state a tolerance for the bug
category_specific_evidence: The bug manifests as a FloatingPointError from jax_debug_nans ("invalid value (nan) encountered in jit(log)") when calling jax.scipy.stats.gamma.pdf inside jax.vmap, not as a numerically wrong result.
The reporter tried jax_enable_x64 and the error persisted, so enabling x64 is not the fix; the passages do not state a dtype for which the defect appears.
The fix in PR#25038 changes gamma.logpdf to compute y via jnp.where(ok, ..., one) and to return jnp.where(ok, log_probs, -jnp.inf), so invalid inputs with x < loc no longer produce internal NaNs.
Invalid inputs with x < loc are documented as returning -inf, which the debug_nans checks were incorrectly flagging.

The regression test testGammaDebugNans wraps gamma.pdf(0.0, 1.0, 1.0) in jax.debug_nans(True) and compares it to scipy with assertAllClose at default tolerance; the passages give no tolerance for the bug itself.
The atol=1E-6 in the passages belongs to the existing testGammaLogPdfZero check, not to the bug, so it is not used as the tolerance here.

The reproduction uses float values around 0.7 to 1.4 for shape/scale and target values near 1.0 on the CPU backend, with jax 0.4.35, jaxlib 0.4.35 and numpy 2.1.3; the passages do not state a magnitude regime where the false positive occurs beyond x < loc inputs.
The passages do not give the PR date, so no date is recorded.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction requires jax_debug_nans to be enabled; without it the NaN error does not appear.
The error surfaces only under jit compilation, and the de-optimized rerun may not reproduce it, so results depend on jit behavior.
The dtype, precision, magnitude regime and tolerance at which the discrepancy appears are not stated in the passages, so these fields are null rather than guessed.
The example mle_loss applies clamp and log to the summed probabilities, so the NaN may originate from log of a zero or negative value rather than from gamma.pdf itself.
